children: UTI Asset Management Company (UTI AMC) reported a 34.4% quarter-on-quarter decline in standalone net profit to ₹143 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹218 crore in the previous quarter.

Revenue fell 23.1% sequentially to ₹337 crore from ₹438 crore. However, core income from the sale of services rose 5% quarter-on-quarter and 2% year-on-year to ₹324 crore, according to exchange filings.

Standalone earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) declined 35% sequentially to ₹195 crore from ₹300 crore. The EBITDA margin narrowed to 57.9% from 68.6% in the previous quarter.

For the first half of FY27, UTI AMC's standalone core income from the sale of services rose 1% year-on-year to ₹632 crore. Core profit after tax increased 14% to ₹253 crore, while overall profit after tax declined 5% to ₹361 crore.

On a consolidated basis, core income from the sale of services grew 1% year-on-year to ₹777 crore in H1 FY27. Core profit after tax rose 15% to ₹263 crore, while overall profit after tax increased 22% to ₹426 crore.
Assets under management and investor participation

UTI Mutual Fund's quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM) stood at ₹4.02 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026. Equity assets, including active and passive investments, accounted for 72% of its total average AUM, compared with an industry average of 62% for equity-oriented assets.
The company's total group AUM stood at ₹16.28 lakh crore, while its live folios reached 1.47 crore as of September 30.
Gross systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows during the quarter stood at ₹2,583 crore. SIP AUM increased 7.82% year-on-year to ₹45,572 crore from ₹42,267 crore as of September 30, 2025.
Digital purchase transactions rose 64.43% year-on-year to 86.74 lakh during the quarter, compared with 52.74 lakh a year earlier. UTI AMC also had a presence across 699 districts in India.
UTI AMC focuses on investor growth under Mission 2031
Commenting on the performance, Vetri Subramaniam, managing director and chief executive officer of UTI AMC, said the company continued to strengthen its franchise and expand investor participation.
He highlighted net inflows of ₹3,415 crore into equity schemes during H1 FY27 and an improvement in the company's share of wallet to 3.82%.
Subramaniam also cited the strength of the company's SIP franchise, increasing digital adoption and a growing investor base as key focus areas under its Mission 2031 strategy.
UTI AMC shares fell 3.07% to ₹825 on October 23, ahead of the company's Q2 FY27 earnings announcement.

title: UTI AMC Q2 results: Net profit falls 34% sequentially to ₹143 crore
